That's a fair read — "he fixes things" and "he said the boarder thing" can both be true. He may fix because it's the only move he knows, not because it's the only move he has.

And there's something useful in what you just said: you're both standing in the same spot. Two people who don't know how to say the thing, so one of you swallows it in the driveway and the other one fixes the sink. Neither of you is actually hiding from the other — you're just both hiding the same way.

You don't have to test him cold. You could give him a small instruction and see what he does with it. Something like: "I'm going to say something and I don't want it fixed. I just want you to hear it." Then say one true, small thing — not the whole driveway sentence, just something real. Watch whether he can sit with it.

If he can, you've learned something. If he can't, you've learned that too — and you'll know what you're working with before you hand him the big one.

What's the smallest true thing you could say that isn't the whole thing?
